title: [P2.10a-hardening-b browser] Control Room generates a session key, signs a Gate 1 request with it, and proves the private key never leaves the browser
description:
PARENT: task-2f554e29d31d48e8a18027110a8e4d5c, whose DoD 3 this row carries. Carried in `dependsOn` as a field so the runtime enforces the order.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ROW. task-2f554e29's own rail 4 says "Split by SPIDR at planning (browser keygen, daemon mint, Control Room signing, bearer retirement) — each row <= 10 files". The parent keeps the DAEMON slice (DoD 2: admit a browser-presented `publicKeySpkiHex` on the approved claim and mint `SessionAuthorityOpened` beside the principal). This row is the BROWSER slice (DoD 3). They are separable because the daemon slice is provable through the listener with a test-generated key, and this row is provable only through a real browser. Nothing was narrowed away — the clause moved to a row that names it.

THE PREREQUISITE THAT MADE THIS POSSIBLE AT ALL ALREADY LANDED. task-d37e8873 (DONE, `751d75a1`) extracted `sessionAuthorityCanonicalString` into `@moe/contracts`, which `apps/control-room` already depends on. Before it, the browser had no way to compute the OPEN_SESSION `requestDigest` and this row was unbuildable — the daemon's canonicalisation lived inside `apps/daemon`, unreachable across the app boundary (no tsconfig `paths`, no project references, deep relative import = TS6059). Compose that module; do NOT write a second canonicalisation.

WHAT THE BROWSER MUST DO, measured from `openSession` (apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority.ts:141-176), not inferred:
1. Generate an Ed25519 keypair with Web Crypto and export SPKI. `clientKeyId` must equal `sessionClientKeyId(publicKeySpkiHex)` — a SHA-256 over the DER — or the mint answers PROOF.
2. Read the three durable operands from `POST /session/challenge-operands/read` (task-c338dd23, DONE at `289507e5`): `recoveryIncarnationRef`, `keyEpochRef`, `profileRevisionId`.
3. Compute `requestDigest` = SHA-256 of `sessionAuthorityCanonicalString({kind:"OPEN_SESSION", projectId, principalId, profileRevisionId, sessionId, credentialId, generation:1, clientKeyId, publicKeySpkiHex, transportId, transportIds})`. The CLIENT chooses `sessionId` and `credentialId` — `openSession` destructures them from its own input at :145-146 and validates with `isBoundedId`. This corrects `comment-3f7a457f`, which claimed the daemon mints them and therefore that no signature could exist before the mint; that was measured against the wrong function.
4. Sign the challenge assembled by `presentedChallenge(selfProof, proof, recovery)`.

ASYNC BOUNDARY, stated because it decides the client's shape: `crypto.subtle.digest` and `crypto.subtle.sign` are Promises, while the daemon's equivalents are synchronous. `sessionAuthorityCanonicalString` is deliberately sync and hash-free precisely so each platform hashes its own way — do not reach for a shared async digest.

DO NOT: put a private key in a request body, a header, a log or storage the DoD's secret sweep can reach; add `node:` builtins to anything the browser loads (Web Crypto only); break task-8aae7ea8's dev-module-graph arm; or edit `budgetRef: hex64("bb")` at live-dispatch-payloads.ts (that literal belongs to task-be80cb74 DoD 4).

The root vitest include has no `apps/**`, so `pnpm test` runs ZERO tests for every file this row touches. Evidence comes from `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and the e2e lane, each with its own count line.

A REAL-BROWSER Playwright arm through the Vite dev module graph, with a NONZERO test count quoted: the Control Room pairs, signs a Gate 1 request with its session key, and stage E's EXISTING signed-proof path authenticates it as HUMAN. SECRET SWEEP: an arm proves the private key never leaves the browser - absent from every request body, every header, every log line, and from any storage the sweep can read. Assert on the captured request/log corpus, not on the absence of a single spelling; a `not.toContain` over one literal tests a spelling, not the property.

FOUR ARMS, TWO OF WHICH ARE THE POINT. Every compared value is COMPUTED on both sides; no hex literal appears in the step, and `grep -nE '"[0-9a-f]{32,}"'` over the module, its suite and the spec EXITs 1. Without (2), (1) is satisfied by any two functions that agree on a single input, including two that ignore their arguments. (3) a `crypto.subtle.sign` signature verifies TRUE through the daemon's real `verifySessionProofOverChallenge`. (4) IT CAN FAIL — a different key is refused FALSE by the same verifier over the same fields.

A browser that SHA-256s the hex STRING produces a well-formed 64-hex clientKeyId that fails only at the mint, with PROOF, and no unit arm would notice — assert the browser's clientKeyId equals the daemon's `sessionClientKeyId` for the same key, computed on both sides, never a spelled literal.
